summary: Markets posted their eighth consecutive weekly gain on hopes of a Middle East peace breakthrough, with the S&P 500 on pace for its longest winning streak since 2023. Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed Chair on May 22 after the Senate confirmed Trump's pick, replacing Jerome Powell who announced he would stay on the board as governor. The April FOMC meeting saw an unusual 8-4 split decision to hold rates at 3.5-3.75%, with elevated inflation tied to the Iran conflict keeping policymakers cautious. Nvidia's Q1 earnings beat expectations on May 21, though shares showed muted reaction in a pattern typical of post-earnings moves for the chip giant. Oil pulled back from four-year highs near $120/barrel on signs of diplomatic progress, while consumer sentiment collapsed to levels last seen during the 2022 trough as energy prices fuel inflation fears. The Dow closed at a new record Friday, while crypto markets traded mixed with Bitcoin holding above $77,000 and Ethereum down nearly 3% amid ETF outflows.

signals.title: Warsh Takes Fed Helm as Powell Era Ends, Policy Outlook Uncertain
signals.desc: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed Chair May 22 with inflation elevated and job growth near zero; market expects more dovish stance but 60% chance of rate hike priced in after April's contentious 8-4 vote.

signals.title: U.S.-Iran Peace Talks Advance, Oil Retreats From 4-Year Highs
signals.desc: President Trump announced an agreement 'largely negotiated' with Iran over the weekend; oil futures fell 5-6% on Wednesday, easing stagflation fears and supporting equities.

signals.title: S&P 500 Extends Win Streak to Eight Weeks, Dow Hits New Record
signals.desc: Major indexes posted weekly gains with the Dow closing at 50,579 on Friday; strong dip-buying and rotation into small-caps and REITs signal broadening market participation.

signals.title: Nvidia Beats Q1 Estimates, Announces Dividend Hike but Shares Flat
signals.desc: Nvidia reported May 21 earnings beat with revenue above $24B but stock showed typical post-results muted reaction; SoftBank and Arm rallied 20%+ on AI momentum spillover.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $1.26B Weekly Outflows, Ethereum Down 3%
signals.desc: Spot Bitcoin ETFs suffered worst weekly drain since January while Ethereum fell 2.99% to $2,058; Harvard fully exited its Ethereum ETF position in Q1 amid broader crypto rotation concerns.

verdict: Markets enter Memorial Day week with bullish momentum intact but facing June headwinds from thin earnings catalysts, hawkish Fed policy risks, and stretched valuations after an historic eight-week run.
